Complex survey analysis

Source: vignettes/survey-analysis.Rmd
survey-analysis.Rmd
library(vaxsurvR)

The design is not optional

A coverage survey is a stratified multi-stage cluster sample with unequal selection probabilities. Ignoring that gives standard errors that are too small, often by a factor of two or more, and – if weights vary – point estimates that are simply wrong for the population.

vaxsurvR does not implement its own variance estimator. vcs_design() builds a survey::svydesign and everything downstream runs on it.

Building the design

With a mapped dataset, the design variables are already standardised, so the call needs no arguments:

d   <- derive_vaccination_status(vcs_example, evidence = "card_or_recall")
des <- vcs_design(d)
des
#> <vcs_design>
#>   records : 256
#>   ids     : psu + segment
#>   strata  : stratum
#>   weights : weight
#>   lonely PSU rule: adjust

Or specify it explicitly:

vcs_design(d, ids = ~psu, strata = ~stratum, weights = ~weight)
#> <vcs_design>
#>   records : 256
#>   ids     : psu
#>   strata  : stratum
#>   weights : weight
#>   lonely PSU rule: adjust

nest = TRUE (the default) tells survey that PSU labels restart within each stratum, which is the usual convention when clusters are numbered per stratum.

No weights is a loud condition, not a quiet one 

no_w <- d
no_w$children$weight <- NULL
no_w$households$weight <- NULL
des_unweighted <- suppressWarnings(vcs_design(no_w))
des_unweighted
#> <vcs_design>
#>   records : 256
#>   ids     : psu + segment
#>   strata  : stratum
#>   weights : .vcs_equal_weight  (equal weights - NOT population estimates)
#>   lonely PSU rule: adjust

The warning and the printed note are deliberate: an unweighted result is a description of the sample, not an estimate for the population, and it should never be reported as coverage.

Checking the weights first 

issues(validate_weights(vcs_example))
#> # A tibble: 30 × 8
#>    check            rule_id      severity level record_id variable value message
#>    <chr>            <chr>        <fct>    <chr> <chr>     <chr>    <chr> <chr>  
#>  1 validate_weights WT_VARIES_I… INFO     surv… PSU001    weight   NA    Weight…
#>  2 validate_weights WT_VARIES_I… INFO     surv… PSU002    weight   NA    Weight…
#>  3 validate_weights WT_VARIES_I… INFO     surv… PSU003    weight   NA    Weight…
#>  4 validate_weights WT_VARIES_I… INFO     surv… PSU004    weight   NA    Weight…
#>  5 validate_weights WT_VARIES_I… INFO     surv… PSU005    weight   NA    Weight…
#>  6 validate_weights WT_VARIES_I… INFO     surv… PSU006    weight   NA    Weight…
#>  7 validate_weights WT_VARIES_I… INFO     surv… PSU007    weight   NA    Weight…
#>  8 validate_weights WT_VARIES_I… INFO     surv… PSU008    weight   NA    Weight…
#>  9 validate_weights WT_VARIES_I… INFO     surv… PSU009    weight   NA    Weight…
#> 10 validate_weights WT_VARIES_I… INFO     surv… PSU010    weight   NA    Weight…
#> # ℹ 20 more rows
check_weight_distribution(vcs_example, by = ~stratum)
#> # A tibble: 2 × 11
#>   group     n n_missing   min   q25 median   q75   max  mean    cv   sum
#>   <chr> <int>     <int> <dbl> <dbl>  <dbl> <dbl> <dbl> <dbl> <dbl> <dbl>
#> 1 rural   126         0 0.833 0.951   1.23  1.49  1.67  1.22 0.214  154.
#> 2 urban   130         0 0.764 0.946   1.31  1.39  1.64  1.20 0.221  156.

The coefficient of variation of the weights matters because it inflates the design effect by roughly 1 + cv^2 regardless of clustering. A survey with a CV of 1 has lost about half its effective sample size to weighting alone.

Trimming

Trimming trades variance for bias. vaxsurvR never trims automatically.

trimmed <- trim_weights(vcs_example, lower = 0.02, upper = 0.98)
c(original = sum(vcs_example$children$weight),
  trimmed  = sum(trimmed$children$weight_trimmed))
#> original  trimmed 
#>  310.365  310.365

The rescaling keeps the weight total unchanged, and the original column stays. The rule is recorded:

subset(derivation_rules(trimmed), variable == "weight_trimmed")$rule
#>                                                                           weight_trimmed 
#> "weight winsorised at the 0.02 and 0.98 quantiles (0.7945, 1.61) and rescaled by 1.0002"

If you trim, say so in the methods section.

Design effects 

design_effect(des, c("cov_BCG", "cov_PENTA1", "cov_PENTA3", "cov_MCV1"))
#> # A tibble: 4 × 5
#>   variable   estimate     se  deff     n
#>   <chr>         <dbl>  <dbl> <dbl> <int>
#> 1 cov_BCG       0.852 0.0235 1.11    253
#> 2 cov_PENTA1    0.907 0.0155 0.716   252
#> 3 cov_PENTA3    0.543 0.0302 0.931   255
#> 4 cov_MCV1      0.608 0.0320 1.08    253

A design effect of 2 means the clustered sample of n children carries about as much information as a simple random sample of n/2. It is the number that tells you whether the sample size was adequate.

Single-PSU strata

A stratum with one PSU has no within-stratum variance to estimate. The behaviour is an argument rather than a global option you have to remember:

lonely <- d
lonely$households$stratum[lonely$households$psu == lonely$households$psu[1]] <- "lonely"

des_lonely <- vcs_design(lonely, lonely_psu = "adjust")
estimate_coverage(des_lonely, vaccines = "BCG")
#> <vcs_estimate: 1 row(s)>
#>   evidence : card_or_recall
#> # A tibble: 1 × 13
#>   indicator domain    numerator denominator estimate     se conf_low conf_high
#>   <chr>     <chr>         <dbl>       <dbl>    <dbl>  <dbl>    <dbl>     <dbl>
#> 1 BCG       <overall>       218         253    0.852 0.0237    0.805     0.898
#> # ℹ 5 more variables: n_unweighted <dbl>, deff <dbl>, neff <dbl>, icc <dbl>,
#> #   ci_method <chr>

"adjust" centres such strata at the grand mean, which is conservative. "fail" refuses to estimate, which is sometimes what you want in a pipeline that should not silently paper over a design problem. The choice is stored on the design and re-applied at every estimate, so it cannot drift.

Domains

Domain estimation subsets the estimator, not the data, so the variance accounts for the fact that domain sample sizes are random.

estimate_coverage(des, vaccines = "PENTA3", by = ~stratum)
#> <vcs_estimate: 2 row(s)>
#>   evidence : card_or_recall
#> # A tibble: 2 × 14
#>   indicator domain stratum numerator denominator estimate     se conf_low
#>   <chr>     <chr>  <chr>       <dbl>       <dbl>    <dbl>  <dbl>    <dbl>
#> 1 PENTA3    rural  rural          52         125    0.423 0.0375    0.349
#> 2 PENTA3    urban  urban          85         130    0.661 0.0448    0.573
#> # ℹ 6 more variables: conf_high <dbl>, n_unweighted <dbl>, deff <dbl>,
#> #   neff <dbl>, icc <dbl>, ci_method <chr>
estimate_coverage(des, vaccines = "BCG", by = c("stratum", "sex"))
#> <vcs_estimate: 4 row(s)>
#>   evidence : card_or_recall
#> # A tibble: 4 × 15
#>   indicator domain   stratum sex   numerator denominator estimate    se conf_low
#>   <chr>     <chr>    <chr>   <chr>     <dbl>       <dbl>    <dbl> <dbl>    <dbl>
#> 1 BCG       rural |… rural   1            44          56    0.772     1        0
#> 2 BCG       urban |… urban   1            46          51    0.884     1        0
#> 3 BCG       rural |… rural   2            58          68    0.847     2        0
#> 4 BCG       urban |… urban   2            70          78    0.895     2        0
#> # ℹ 6 more variables: conf_high <dbl>, n_unweighted <dbl>, deff <dbl>,
#> #   neff <dbl>, icc <dbl>, ci_method <chr>

Reading the output

Every estimate table carries the same columns:

Column Meaning
numerator, denominator unweighted counts a reader can recount
estimate design-based weighted proportion
se design-based standard error
conf_low, conf_high confidence limits, clipped to [0, 1]
n_unweighted children contributing to the estimate
deff design effect where estimable

Where the design gives no usable standard error – a domain with a single cluster, say – a Wilson interval takes over rather than the row being blank.

Reaching the rest of the survey package 

svy <- as_survey_design(des)
survey::svyby(~cov_PENTA3, ~stratum, svy, survey::svymean, na.rm = TRUE)
#>       stratum cov_PENTA3         se
#> rural   rural  0.4228441 0.03751362
#> urban   urban  0.6610834 0.04484090

Anything vaxsurvR does not wrap is one call away.
